placements.role: Provides large-scale electrical transmission, distribution and substation construction services.

role_evidence.claim: MYR Group's 2025 Form 10-K says its Transmission and Distribution segment designs, engineers, builds, upgrades and repairs transmission networks, distribution systems and substations.

business_summary: MYR Group Inc. is a Nasdaq-listed holding company for specialty electrical contractors in the United States and Canada. Its Transmission and Distribution segment builds and maintains transmission lines, distribution systems and substations for electric utilities; its Commercial and Industrial segment does electrical construction for buildings including data centres. It is a labour and execution business, not a manufacturer, so its margins are contract margins.

exposure_summary.narrative: MYR Group has one placement, on grid-interconnect, position three of the chain and the link the chain's own bottleneck note calls the slowest step in the entire sequence. The link is scored UNDISCOVERED with the lowest crowdedness score on the chain. The company's exposure is double-sided: the T&D segment builds the interconnection itself, and the C&I segment names data centres as one of the facility types it wires.

disposition.basis: Complete medium profile on the quietest link of the chain, with the fullest measurement set after Vertiv: every canonical field sourced, Piotroski at the top of its range and Beneish clean. confidence_audit.basis: Counts cover the canonical metric fields only. VERIFIED is a figure read directly off SEC companyfacts as reported. INFERRED is a figure computed from SEC companyfacts, with the derivation named in its basis; where a market price enters the computation the basis says so explicitly, because the price leg is the repo's own dual-source market plane (data/market/MYRG.json, price_status AGREED) and not an issuer document. SPECULATIVE is reserved for the reverse-DCF solve, whose discount rate and terminal growth are assumed. NULL is a field looked for and not found, never estimated.

direct_exposure.basis: One ACTIVE, role-evidenced placement in the PASS-audited mapping, on grid-interconnect, position three of twelve. The mapped role evidence is MYR Group's 2025 Form 10-K: the Transmission and Distribution segment designs, engineers, builds, upgrades and repairs transmission networks, distribution systems and substations. The chain's own bottleneck note calls this link the slowest step in the entire chain, so the exposure is to the gate on data-centre energization rather than to accelerator demand itself.
direct_exposure.second_side: The Commercial and Industrial segment names data centres among the facility types it wires, which is a second, building-side exposure to the same occurrence.

disclosed_theme_revenue_pct.basis: No data-centre-attributable revenue percentage is disclosed. The fetched Q2 2026 8-K exhibit (accession 0000700923-26-000041) reports revenue by T&D and C&I segment only. The exposure argument therefore rests on segment role and link position, not on a disclosed share, and this is the single largest measurement weakness in the promotion.

capture.basis: This is the dimension that argues against the name, and it is recorded as such rather than netted away. The chain scores capture at 40 on grid-interconnect and its rationale names the link as the chain's trap example: much of it is regulated-return or competitively bid EPC, volume without proportional profit capture, and it is un-crowded partly because capture is capped. MYR Group is a contractor to utilities and facility owners, so it earns the labour and execution margin on interconnection, not the equipment margin. Operating margin of 4.562 percent for the fiscal year ended 2025-12-31 (OperatingIncomeLoss 166872000 over Revenues 3657889000, SEC companyfacts) is consistent with a bid-competed contract business.
capture.what_would_change_it: A disclosed data-centre or large-load revenue share, or a sustained operating-margin step up on flat revenue, would separate execution scarcity from ordinary EPC bidding. Neither exists on disk today.

heat.basis: Ember scores grid-interconnect UNDISCOVERED: impact 70 on time-to-power being the stated gating factor for new capacity, crowdedness 30 (the lowest on this chain, rationale calling it the quietest corner in retail terms), capture 40. It is not the chain's money corner; power-equipment is, and this promotion does not claim otherwise.

issuer_attention_conflict.basis: The two PCS axes disagree on this issuer and the disagreement is stated rather than resolved in the flattering direction. Axis A reads DARK at 73.5 on three retail-attention sub-scores (trends 12, wsb 25, stocktwits 13, media null) and Axis B reads SATURATED on institutional coverage in the same block. Axis A is ADVISORY per method section 3, and its gate in data/market/MYRG.json records the reason as unreadable positive-control fixtures, so it is running without its own control. The honest reading is that retail chatter is thin while institutional coverage is not absent, and the link-level crowdedness score of 30 is a chain judgment about the corner, not a measurement of this issuer. Neither axis alone carries the promotion.

quality.basis: Every canonical metric field on this profile resolves to a sourced number and none is NULL, which is true of only two of the six complete profiles in this campaign. Piotroski 8 (STRONG) and Beneish -2.206 (CLEAN) both compute from complete inputs in data/market/MYRG.json quality; there is no companyfacts coverage gap on this filer. Net debt to EBITDA is -0.5705, a net cash balance sheet, computed from total debt 4722000 less cash 137872000 as of 2026-06-30 over an EBITDA proxy of 233384000 for the fiscal year ended 2025-12-31, and its basis states that it mixes the latest instant against the last full fiscal year.
quality.counterweight: Operating cash flow to net income of 2.7578 is the highest in this batch and is not read as quality: for a contractor that is usually working-capital timing rather than durable conversion, and the profile's own risk block says so. The companyfacts operating income series also shows fiscal 2024 at roughly half of fiscal 2023 before recovering in fiscal 2025 on broadly flat revenue, so contract margin has been volatile.

expectations_gap.basis: The reverse DCF in data/market/MYRG.json quality.reverse_dcf solves a 7.0 percent free-cash-flow CAGR over a five-year explicit period on base FCF 232195000 at a 0.09 discount rate and 0.025 terminal growth. The achieved three-year revenue CAGR to the fiscal year ended 2025-12-31 is 6.7312 percent from the companyfacts Revenues series. The implied bar therefore sits at roughly the growth rate the company has already delivered, which is the cheapest expectations bar among the six complete profiles in this campaign and is the reason the name is worth a dive rather than a monitoring slot.
expectations_gap.horizon_caveat: The horizon spread is 1.95 percentage points (7.0 percent at five years against 5.05 percent at ten from the same price and base cash flow). Per method section 7 a gap smaller than that spread is a statement about the horizon convention, not about the price. Any gap Stocky claims on this name must be larger than 1.95 points or must say which of the two it is claiming.
expectations_gap.assumption_caveat: The discount rate and terminal growth are assumed, so both reverse-DCF fields are tagged SPECULATIVE in the profile confidence audit. This dimension records the measured expectation state and the size of the horizon artefact; it does not adjudicate whether the price is wrong. That is the deep-dive stage's work and no verdict is written here.
